frames.narration: A cart holds three prices in cents: 1,000, 2,500 and 400. A header badge, a summary and an email all read it, and each asks a helper for the total with a 10 percent coupon.

The helper applies the coupon to the cart's own list, then sums it. The badge shows 3,510. The summary calls it again and the coupon is applied a second time: 3,159. The email gets 2,842. One cart, three totals, and no widget did anything wrong.
The fix is a pure helper: it computes the discounted total from the list and returns it, without changing the list. All three widgets now show 3,510, in any order and any number of calls.

Now the cart can have 10,000 items, and every update must build a new value. Copying all of it on each update means 100 updates cost 1,000,000 element copies. In-place edits cost 100 writes. Safe, but 10,000 times the work.

Structural sharing keeps the cart as a tree of 32-slot nodes, copies only the nodes from the root to the changed item and shares the rest. In this model, 10,000 items need 3 levels, 96 copies per update, 9,600 for the 100 updates. Old versions stay valid.

It is not free for small data. With 10 items and 100 updates, copying everything costs 1,000 copies and structural sharing 3,200, because it always copies a whole node. In this model it pays off only from 65 items.

Mutation is fine where nobody can see it. Copy the cart once, update the private copy 100 times in a loop, and hand it out as a finished value: 10,100 copies for 10,000 items, and no reader ever sees a half-updated cart.
So: make shared values and function results immutable, update by building a new value, share the parts that did not change, and keep in-place mutation for private data in loops and builders.
